newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco says ruling backs mine leases.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco says ruling backs mine leases.

text.p: Comalco Ltd said on Monday that the validity of the company's bauxite leases at Weipa, Queensland, were confirmed by an Australian High Court ruling that found that the granting of a pastoral lease did not automatically extinguish Aboriginal land claims.

Comalco said in a statement that although the ramifications of the High Court judgement on the Wik case were yet to be analysed in detail, the judgement confirmed the validity of the company's bauxite leases.
"Regardless of the company's technical legal rights, Comalco will continue to negotiate in good faith with the Aboriginal people in the Weipa rea for mutual benefit," Comalco said.
The High Court found that the claim by an Aboriginal group, the Wik, over 35,000 square km of land in Queensland may in some cases extinguish the rights of the 12 pastoral leaseholders in that area.
The judgement was split four-to-three in favour of the Wik people's claim.
A judgment last January in Australia's Federal Court had found that pastoral leases took precedence over Aboriginal land claims, allowing Comalco to mine the bauxite, discovered in the mid-1950s.
The Wik then appealed against the decision.
Comalco is 67 percent owned by RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd.
